column1: # Extensions that Dixlase Core integration-tests in CI.
# Format: <directory-name>\t<git-url>
# Comments start with '#' and are skipped.
# Each extension listed here is shallow-cloned into plugins/<dir-name>/ by
# .github/scripts/fetch-integration-plugins.sh at the start of every CI
# run that needs the bundled extensions (test.yml's plugin-tests /
# migration / migration-lint / comment-translation-status,
# plugin-api-check.yml, generated-docs-drift.yml).
# This file lists only the extensions this repository distributes
# publicly. Core is integration-tested against more than these, and the
# rows for the rest are held in the INTEGRATION_EXTENSIONS repository (or
# organisation) variable, which the fetch script merges with this file at
# run time. The reason is dixlase-core#619: a public repository should not
# publish the names and the directory layout of software its readers
# cannot obtain, and the files that define how the project is built and
# tested are the last place that should do it by accident. A fork has no
# token to clone them with either, so it gets exactly this list.
# That variable's rows carry two extra columns the fetch script reads —
# a test tier and a flag field. Its own header documents them.
# This file replaced the per-extension entries that used to live in
# .gitmodules. The motivation was that `git clone` of dixlase-core
# unavoidably creates an empty placeholder directory for every gitlink
# in the tree, even when --no-recurse-submodules is passed — so a plain
# clone left plugins/ littered with empty directories. The fix is to
# keep the integration list outside git's submodule machinery: fresh
# clones leave plugins/ empty, the install wizard / dls:plugin:install
# fetch real extensions on demand for operators, and this TSV is the
# canonical list for CI to clone for integration testing.
# Adding a publicly distributed extension:
#   1. Append a row here.
#   2. If it ships PHPUnit tests, register its testsuite in phpunit.xml
#      so test.yml's plugin-tests job can select it.
#   3. Name it in the appropriate tier of test.yml's --testsuite=
#      arguments (well-tested / moderate / minimal).
# Adding one that is not distributed publicly: append a row to the
# INTEGRATION_EXTENSIONS variable instead, with its tier. The fetch
# script registers the testsuite and places it in the tier for you —
# nothing is added to this file or to phpunit.xml.
# Removing a publicly distributed extension:
#   1. Delete its row here.
#   2. Drop the matching testsuite from phpunit.xml and the --testsuite=
#      string in test.yml.
